rich_summary: As Shatrughna battles the demon Lavana, the gods gather in the sky to witness the climactic moment. Shatrughna unleashes a radiant celestial weapon whose brilliance resembles the fire that ends the universe. His arrow pierces Lavana’s chest, descends even into the netherworld, and then returns to its master; the demon collapses like a mountain struck by lightning. With the terror of the three worlds destroyed, the gods rejoice and offer Shatrughna a boon. He asks to rule the beautiful city built by the gods, and they grant it, naming it Shurashena. Shatrughna summons his army and establishes prosperous rule there. For twelve peaceful years the land flourishes under his protection, until he finally longs to see his brother Rama again, prompting a future return to Ayodhya.

highlight_spans.why: The gathering of the gods and the cosmic brilliance of Shatrughna’s weapon frame the battle as a moment of divine significance.
Description of Shatrughna’s flourishing city on the Yamuna shows the transformation from demon‑haunted land to prosperous kingdom.

top_scenes.scene_text: Shatrughna releases a blazing celestial arrow as the sky fills with gods watching, the weapon streaking downward toward the demon Lavana.
Lavana collapsing like a lightning‑struck mountain while the divine hosts hover in the heavens above the battlefield.
The radiant city of Shurashena rising on the banks of the Yamuna, filled with markets, temples, and gardens under Shatrughna’s prosperous rule.
